title: Sher Singh and the ministers
hook: a new Maharaja, a court full of rivals, and a gun held out as a gift

segments.voice: Yesterday, two heirs in a year, Kharak Singh and his son, and your line was power is fragile. Where did you see something strong turn out to be thin? Today, the next man to sit on that fragile throne. Day nine hundred twenty-seven.

A courtier walks across a garden toward the Maharaja, carrying a new gun. He's come, the story goes, to show it off. A fine piece, worth a look. The Maharaja reaches for it. In the histories of Lahore, that moment is where the court's long quarrel stops being whispers and becomes blood. The man on the throne is Sher Singh, a son of Ranjit Singh. The man with the gun belongs to a family he had welcomed back to court. Today: Sher Singh and the ministers.
screen: `A COURTIER WITH A NEW GUN.` → `THE MAHARAJA REACHES FOR IT.` → `SHER SINGH, SON OF RANJIT SINGH.`

segments.voice: First, the throne. After the two heirs you met yesterday, Sher Singh came to power through a hard struggle with rivals inside the royal family. He was brave and easygoing, the histories say, fond of hunting and company, and less fond of the hard, daily work of holding a court together. Second, the ministers. Around him stood the men who really ran things. Dhian Singh, the Dogra chief minister, you met at the court of many faiths. Against him stood the Sandhawalia sardars, kin of the royal house, with their own claims and grudges. Each side watched the other. Each wanted the Maharaja's ear. Third, the day it broke. The Sandhawalias had fallen out with the court and later been brought back into favor. Then, as Cunningham and other histories tell it, Ajit Singh Sandhawalia came to Sher Singh with a gun to show him, and shot him with it. The Maharaja's young son Partap Singh was killed the same day. And before the day was over, the Sandhawalias killed Dhian Singh too, the minister some accounts say had been in on the plot with them. Then Dhian Singh's son, Hira Singh, turned the army against them, and they were killed in turn. One plot, and a whole circle of men were dead. Fourth, what the Gurus had said about it. In the first pauri, or stanza, of the Japji, Guru Nanak asks how a person can become truthful, and how the wall of falsehood can be torn down. His answer is to walk in the Lord's will. Intrigue is falsehood made into a plan. It promises a safe path to power, and at Lahore it ended in a garden, a gun, and a line of graves. That's today's line.
screen: `A BRAVE, EASYGOING MAHARAJA.` · `MINISTERS WATCHING EACH OTHER.` · `ONE PLOT, A CIRCLE OF DEAD MEN.` · `THE WALL OF FALSEHOOD.` · then, large: `INTRIGUE KILLS.`

segments.voice: Two minutes away from the whispers. Sit, and let your breath settle. Bring to mind one place in your life where quiet sides are forming: a group chat, an office, a family argument, a team. Notice who's talking about whom. Notice whether you've been pulled in, even a little. Now picture yourself stepping back from it, one step, not cold and not superior, just out. Breathe there for a while. If you pray, you can say Waheguru on each breath out. The bell holds the time.
Sher Singh, a son of Ranjit Singh, caught in a court split between rival families, and killed along with his son and his chief minister in a plot. Today's word.
Your line: intrigue kills. Today, stay out of one intrigue. When the whisper comes your way, don't pass it on. Day nine hundred twenty-seven.

screen: `DAY 927 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: A CHILD ON THE THRONE.`

howItsDone: Sikh histories remember the killing of Maharaja Sher Singh as part of the court intrigues that weakened the kingdom after Ranjit Singh, and Sikhs often point to the Gurus' warnings against falsehood when they tell it.

fork.setup: you're Sher Singh. a family that once quarreled with the court has come back into favor. one of them crosses the garden with a new gun to show you. what happens, as the histories tell it?

fork.reveal: Ajit Singh Sandhawalia shot the Maharaja with the gun he'd brought to show him; the killing spread to his son and his chief minister.

original.note: koor, falsehood; in the Japji's first pauri, Guru Nanak asks how the wall of falsehood can be torn down.

trapdoor: what you thought: the kingdom fell to an enemy army.
what it means: after Ranjit Singh, his court turned on itself, and Sher Singh was killed by men he had welcomed back.
what a scholar hears: one plot killed a Maharaja, his son and his chief minister, and the revenge that followed left the army stronger than the court.
